name: 20 · Explaining processes and next steps · Natural English
description: 100 microescenarios para explicar procesos, secuencias, responsabilidades, requisitos, progreso, traspasos, plazos, acciones, bloqueos y próximos pasos con un inglés claro, natural y profesional. El contexto SOC sirve de apoyo; las respuestas se deciden por gramática, colocación, claridad, tono y nivel de certeza, no por conocimientos técnicos discutibles.

questions.question: At the start of a briefing, you want to introduce the end-to-end review workflow. What is the clearest way to begin?
options: Let me tell the process from the beginning to the ending in every detail.
I will walk the review process so you can know all of its functioning.
Let me walk you through how the review process works from start to finish.
Let me explain you how the review process works since its start until its finish.
questions.explanation: «Walk someone through» es una expresión natural para explicar un proceso paso a paso. «Explain» necesita «to» delante de la persona, y «from start to finish» es la fórmula idiomática.
questions.translation: Permíteme explicarte cómo funciona el proceso de revisión de principio a fin.

questions.question: Complete the sentence: 'The purpose of this initial check is ___.'
options: to confirm that we have the information needed to begin the analysis
to confirm us that the information is enough for beginning to analyze
confirming that we have the information needed for begin the analysis
that we confirm having all information before to begin the analysis
questions.explanation: Después de «the purpose ... is», «to + infinitive» expresa la finalidad de forma clara. «Needed to begin» evita las construcciones incorrectas «for begin» y «before to begin».
questions.translation: El objetivo de esta comprobación inicial es confirmar que tenemos la información necesaria para comenzar el análisis.

questions.question: A customer asks what happens after a ticket is created. Choose the most natural overview.
options: Once the ticket is created, it is reviewed, assigned and prioritized.
After creating the ticket, there is made its review, assignment and priority.
Once the ticket will be created, it reviews, assigns and prioritizes.
When the ticket is creating, it will be reviewed, assigned and given prioritization.
questions.explanation: En una cláusula temporal con «once» se usa presente simple, no «will». La serie de pasivas «is reviewed, assigned and prioritized» es paralela y natural.
questions.translation: Una vez creado el ticket, se revisa, se asigna y se prioriza.

questions.question: Which sentence gives a concise high-level description of the process?
options: On high level, there are three process stages, being validation, investigation and following.
At a high level, the process has three stages: validation, investigation and follow-up.
At a high level, the process makes three stages that validate, investigate and follow.
In a high level, the process is composed by validation, investigation and the follow-up.
questions.explanation: La colocación correcta es «at a high level». «Consists of» o «has» son naturales; «is composed by» no lo es en este contexto.
questions.translation: A grandes rasgos, el proceso tiene tres etapas: validación, investigación y seguimiento.

questions.question: You want to reassure the customer without promising a specific outcome. Which sentence is best?
options: The process guarantees that every case will always have the same final result.
The process assures a successful outcome for all cases that enter into review.
The process is designed for ensuring each case to receive an identical conclusion.
The process is designed to ensure that each case receives a consistent review.
questions.explanation: «Is designed to ensure» expresa el objetivo del proceso sin garantizar resultados. «Consistent review» significa un enfoque coherente, no una conclusión idéntica.
questions.translation: El proceso está diseñado para garantizar que cada caso reciba una revisión coherente.

questions.question: A diagram contains many details. How would you introduce it in a customer-friendly way?
options: The diagram teaches the main steps, and the details can be watched during the advance.
This diagram is showing all steps, and we can see the details while we will go.
In this diagram are shown the principal steps for looking details progressively.
This diagram shows the main steps; we can look at the details as we go.
questions.explanation: «Shows the main steps» usa presente simple para describir un gráfico. «As we go» es una expresión oral natural para indicar que los detalles se tratarán progresivamente.
questions.translation: Este diagrama muestra los pasos principales; podemos ver los detalles a medida que avanzamos.

questions.question: Which phrase best signals that you are simplifying a complex workflow?
options: In simple terms, we verify the request, carry out the work and report the outcome.
In simple words, we verify the request, realize the work and inform about the result.
Saying it easily, the request is verified, the work gets made and the outcome reports.
For simplifying, we do a verification, an execution and an information of results.
questions.explanation: «In simple terms» es un marcador natural. «Carry out the work» y «report the outcome» son colocaciones idiomáticas; «realize the work» es una traducción literal incorrecta.
questions.translation: Dicho de forma sencilla, verificamos la solicitud, realizamos el trabajo e informamos del resultado.

questions.question: You need to distinguish the standard process from possible exceptions. Which sentence is clearest?
options: This is the standard process, despite some cases may require additional checks.
This is the standard process, although some cases may require additional checks.
This standard process applies always, except that extra checks will be definitely required.
This is the process by standard, although some cases can require checks in addition.
questions.explanation: «Although» introduce correctamente una oración completa. «Despite» necesitaría un sustantivo o gerundio. «May require» mantiene un nivel de certeza adecuado.
questions.translation: Este es el proceso estándar, aunque algunos casos pueden requerir comprobaciones adicionales.

questions.question: A colleague has already explained the technical details. You only need to summarize the workflow. What should you say?
options: For resume, the request assesses first and later passes to the team that corresponds.
To make a summary, the request has assessment before passing it toward an appropriate team.
To summarize, the request is assessed first and then passed to the appropriate team.
Summarizing it, first is assessed the request and after is passed to the adequate team.
questions.explanation: «To summarize» introduce un resumen con naturalidad. La pasiva «is assessed ... and then passed» mantiene el paralelismo; «for resume» es un falso amigo.
questions.translation: En resumen, la solicitud se evalúa primero y luego se remite al equipo adecuado.

questions.question: Which sentence best explains where the customer's part of the process begins?
options: The part of you begins in the moment where our findings are sent for your revision.
Your part starts from that we send the findings to be reviewed by your side.
Your part begins when we will send the findings for review.
Your part begins when we send you the findings for review.
questions.explanation: Tras «when» con sentido futuro se usa presente simple. «Send you the findings for review» es conciso y «review» significa revisión; «revision» suele tener otro sentido.
questions.translation: Su parte comienza cuando les enviamos los hallazgos para que los revisen.

questions.question: You are describing the first two steps of an access review. Which version is most natural?
options: First, we confirm the scope. Then, we collect the relevant records.
At first, we are confirming the scope, and in a second time records get collected.
Firstly we confirm about the scope, and after we collect the records that are relevant.
Firstly, confirm the scope; after, collect the relevant records.
questions.explanation: «First ... Then ...» es la secuencia más clara en inglés oral. «Confirm the scope» no lleva «about», y «records» evita el falso amigo «registers».
questions.translation: Primero confirmamos el alcance. Después recopilamos los registros pertinentes.

questions.question: Complete the transition: '___ the data has been validated, the analyst can begin the review.'
options: Despite
During
Once
Until
questions.explanation: «Once» significa «una vez que» e introduce la condición temporal que debe cumplirse. «During» necesita un sustantivo, «until» cambia la relación temporal y «despite» expresa contraste.
questions.translation: Una vez validados los datos, el analista puede comenzar la revisión.

questions.question: Which sentence explains two actions that happen at the same time?
options: Meanwhile the evidence review, the coordinator maintains informed the customer.
While the analyst will review the evidence, the coordinator is keeping updated to the customer.
While the analyst reviews the evidence, the coordinator keeps the customer updated.
During the analyst reviews the evidence, the coordinator keeps the customer updated.
questions.explanation: «While + oración» expresa simultaneidad. «During» debe ir seguido de un sustantivo, y la colocación correcta es «keep someone updated».
questions.translation: Mientras el analista revisa las pruebas, el coordinador mantiene informado al cliente.

questions.question: You need to explain that one step must finish before another starts. Choose the clearest sentence.
options: We need to complete the validation before we move on to the investigation.
We need to finish with validation before that we can pass toward investigation.
Before to move on the investigation, the validation needs being completed by us.
We need completing the validation before moving us to the investigation.
questions.explanation: «Complete ... before we move on to ...» combina estructuras naturales. «Move on to» lleva «to», y después de «before» no se usa «to + infinitive» en esta construcción.
questions.translation: Tenemos que completar la validación antes de pasar a la investigación.

questions.question: A process returns to an earlier step when information is missing. Which sentence sounds best?
options: When information will miss, we go again to the requester to clarify us.
In case of missing informations, the process comes backward for requester clarification.
If information is missing, we go back to the requester for clarification.
If an information is missing, we return back with the requester for clarifying.
questions.explanation: «Information» es incontable y no admite «an» ni plural. «Go back to someone for clarification» es una expresión clara y natural.
questions.translation: Si falta información, volvemos a contactar con el solicitante para pedir una aclaración.

questions.question: Which transition introduces the final stage without sounding abrupt?
options: For finishing, the outcome gets documented and the request is put as closed.
Finally, documentate the outcome and close the request.
At the end, we make the documentation of the outcome and we give closure to the request.
Finally, we document the outcome and close the request.
questions.explanation: «Finally» presenta el último paso. «Document the outcome» y «close the request» son verbos directos; «documentate» no existe y «make the documentation» resulta pesado.
questions.translation: Por último, documentamos el resultado y cerramos la solicitud.

questions.question: You want to insert an optional step into the sequence. Which sentence is most natural?
options: If it would be necessary, we can make a pause in this point for requesting more evidences.
If necessary, pause here for request further evidence.
If necessary, we may pause at this point to request further evidence.
If needed perhaps, the process will stop itself at this point to solicit further proofs.
questions.explanation: «If necessary» y «at this point» son fórmulas naturales. «Evidence» es incontable y «may» indica posibilidad sin presentar la pausa como automática.
questions.translation: Si es necesario, podemos detenernos en este punto para solicitar pruebas adicionales.

questions.question: A customer asks what happens immediately after approval. Choose the best reply.
options: So soon the approval is received, implementation scheduling of the change is made.
As soon as approval is received, the change is scheduled for implementation.
As soon as approval will be received, the change schedules for its implementation.
Immediately after to receive approval, we schedule the change for being implemented.
questions.explanation: «As soon as» se combina con presente simple para hablar del futuro. La pasiva «is scheduled for implementation» es precisa y natural.
questions.translation: En cuanto se recibe la aprobación, se programa la implantación del cambio.

questions.question: Which sentence clearly marks a handoff between stages?
options: At that point, the case moves from triage to detailed analysis.
In that point, the case moves toward detailed analysis.
At that moment is when the case moves itself from triage into analyzing detailedly.
In that point, the case passes of triage toward the detailed analysis.
questions.explanation: La expresión correcta es «at that point». «Moves from X to Y» señala la transición de forma sencilla y «detailed» es el adjetivo adecuado.
questions.translation: En ese momento, el caso pasa del triaje al análisis detallado.

questions.question: You are correcting a slide with too many uses of 'then'. Which alternative is best?
options: The records get checked. As next, they are comparing with what was requested originally.
The records are checked. The next step is to compare them with the original request.
The records are checked. In continuation, a comparison with the original requesting is performed.
The records are checked. The following step consists to compare them against the petition original.
questions.explanation: «The next step is to + infinitive» evita repetir «then» y organiza el discurso. «Original request» tiene el orden natural de adjetivo y sustantivo.
questions.translation: Se comprueban los registros. El siguiente paso es compararlos con la solicitud original.

questions.question: You need to explain who performs the initial review. Which sentence is clearest?
options: The service desk carries out the initial review before assigning the case.
The service desk realizes the initial review before to assign the case.
The service desk makes the first revision before that the case is being assigned.
The initial review is responsibility from the service desk prior the case assignment.
questions.explanation: «Carry out a review» es una colocación natural. «Realize» no significa «realizar» en este contexto, y «before» va seguido de gerundio o de una oración.
questions.translation: El service desk realiza la revisión inicial antes de asignar el caso.

questions.question: Complete the customer update: 'Our team is responsible ___ coordinating the investigation.'
options: Our team is responsible of coordinating the investigation.
Our team is responsible to coordinating the investigation.
Our team is responsible in coordinating the investigation.
Our team is responsible for coordinating the investigation.
questions.explanation: La preposición que sigue a «responsible» es «for», y después se usa gerundio: «responsible for coordinating».
questions.translation: Nuestro equipo es responsable de coordinar la investigación.

questions.question: Which sentence assigns a customer action politely and clearly?
options: We will need your team to confirm whether the listed accounts are still active.
We will need that your team confirms us if the listed accounts continue actives.
We need from your team the confirmation about if listed accounts remain being active.
Your team must confirm immediately whether are the accounts still in activity.
questions.explanation: «Need someone to do something» es la estructura correcta. «Whether ... are still active» formula la comprobación con claridad y sin un tono innecesariamente brusco.
questions.translation: Necesitaremos que su equipo confirme si las cuentas indicadas siguen activas.

questions.question: You want to clarify that approval belongs to the customer, not the SOC. Choose the best wording.
options: We can recommend, but the final approval corresponds to be made by your team.
We can make a recommendation, but the final approval rests with your team.
We can make a recommendation, but your team is who has to approve finally.
We can give an advice, although the definitive approbation depends of your team.
questions.explanation: «The final approval rests with...» expresa responsabilidad de forma profesional. «Advice» es incontable, «approbation» no es el término habitual y «depends» llevaría «on».
questions.translation: Podemos hacer una recomendación, pero la aprobación final corresponde a su equipo.

questions.question: Two teams contribute at different points. Which wording describes their shared responsibility most naturally?
options: From our side is the investigation, and from your side is to give the business context.
We investigate the alert while your team provide business context.
We take charge of investigating while your team is in charge to provide business context to us.
We will investigate the alert, while your team provides the business context.
questions.explanation: La estructura paralela con «we ... while your team ...» reparte funciones con claridad. «Provide us with» sería posible, pero «provide us the context» no es estándar.
questions.translation: Nosotros investigaremos la alerta, mientras que su equipo aportará el contexto de negocio.

questions.question: A participant asks who owns the next action. What is the most natural reply?
options: The next action sits with us, and we will update you by Thursday.
The next action is ours; we update you until Thursday.
The ownership of next action belongs to us, and we will inform you in Thursday.
We have the next action under our responsibility and will actualize you by the Thursday.
questions.explanation: «The action sits with us» es una fórmula profesional para indicar responsable. «By Thursday» marca el plazo límite; «until» tendría otro sentido.
questions.translation: La siguiente acción nos corresponde a nosotros y les informaremos a más tardar el jueves.

questions.question: You need to introduce a specialist's role without implying that they lead the whole process. Which sentence is best?
options: The network specialist supports with the team and directs the whole process of checks.
A network specialist will support the team during the connectivity checks.
A network specialist will assist to the team during checks.
A specialist of networks will assist to the team while the checks of connection.
questions.explanation: «Support the team during...» describe una función de apoyo sin exagerarla. «Responsible» no se usa como sustantivo de esa forma y «assist» no lleva «to» ante la persona.
questions.translation: Un especialista de redes apoyará al equipo durante las comprobaciones de conectividad.

questions.question: Which request for an owner sounds collaborative rather than accusatory?
options: Could we agree who will take ownership of this action?
Who is going to be responsible because nobody has taken this action?
Could we accord who owns this action?
Can you say who must own this action that remains without responsible?
questions.explanation: «Could we agree...» incluye a todos y suaviza la petición. «Take ownership of an action» es la colocación natural; «property» no significa responsabilidad.
questions.translation: ¿Podríamos acordar quién se hará responsable de esta acción?

questions.question: A customer has sent the requested logs. How should you acknowledge their role?
options: Thank you for providing the logs; we can now continue with the analysis.
Thank you to provide the logs; now we can follow with the analysis.
Thanks for your logs provisioning; actually we can continue forward the analysis.
We thank you for sending us the logs, so the analysis can be continued by our side now.
questions.explanation: Después de «thank you for» se usa gerundio. «Continue with the analysis» es natural; «actually» significa «en realidad», no «actualmente».
questions.translation: Gracias por facilitar los registros; ahora podemos continuar con el análisis.

questions.question: You are documenting responsibilities after a meeting. Which sentence is most concise?
options: The SOC drafts; the customer makes the revision.
The SOC will draft the report, and the customer will review it.
The SOC will elaborate the report, while the customer will make a revision of the same.
The drafting of the report will be done by the SOC, and its revision will be done by the customer.
questions.explanation: Dos cláusulas activas y paralelas hacen la frase más directa. En pasiva, los agentes llevarían «by», no «from» ni «for».
questions.translation: El SOC redactará el informe y el cliente lo revisará.

questions.question: You are explaining what is needed before an investigation can start. Which sentence is best?
options: Before we can to begin, we are needing the ticket number plus the time rank.
Before beginning, we need that you give us the ticket number and relevant range of time.
Before we begin, we need the ticket number and the relevant time range.
Previous to start, the number of ticket and the temporal range are necessities.
questions.explanation: «Before we begin» y «we need...» son estructuras directas. «Time range» es la colocación correcta; «time rank» y «previous to start» no son naturales.
questions.translation: Antes de empezar, necesitamos el número de ticket y el intervalo de tiempo pertinente.

questions.question: Complete the sentence: 'We cannot proceed ___ the request has been approved.'
options: We cannot proceed until the request has been approved.
We cannot proceed during the request has been approved.
We cannot proceed meanwhile the request has been approved.
We cannot proceed unless of the request has been approved.
questions.explanation: «Not ... until» significa que la acción no puede continuar antes de que se cumpla la condición. Las otras opciones no encajan gramaticalmente.
questions.translation: No podemos continuar hasta que se haya aprobado la solicitud.

questions.question: Which sentence asks for missing information in the most professional way?
options: Could you provide the affected hostname and the approximate start time?
Could you facilitate the hostname and approximate start time?
Could you facilitate us the affected host name and the hour approximately of beginning?
Can you send us which is the hostname affected and when it started more or less?
questions.explanation: «Could you provide...» formula una petición profesional. «Approximate start time» sigue el orden natural del inglés y evita traducciones literales.
questions.translation: ¿Podrían facilitar el nombre del host afectado y la hora aproximada de inicio?

questions.question: The process can start with partial information, but more details will be needed later. Choose the clearest explanation.
options: We can begin with the information available, but later more details will be surely necessary.
We can start from available informations, although we can need further detail while the review will progress.
We can begin with the information available, but we may need further details as the review progresses.
With the information that is available we initiate, but new details could be demanded along the review.
questions.explanation: «Information» es incontable y «as the review progresses» expresa evolución. «May need» mantiene la cautela sin afirmar que siempre harán falta más datos.
questions.translation: Podemos empezar con la información disponible, pero quizá necesitemos más detalles a medida que avance la revisión.

questions.question: You need to explain why accurate contact details matter. Which sentence sounds most natural?
options: Updated contacts help us reach to the right person.
Contacts that are updated permit reaching to the adequate person with no retard.
The current contact data makes easier that we reach the person who corresponds rapidly.
Up-to-date contact details help us reach the right person without delay.
questions.explanation: «Up-to-date contact details» es la expresión idiomática. «Reach someone» no lleva «to» y «actualized» es una traducción literal poco natural.
questions.translation: Unos datos de contacto actualizados nos ayudan a localizar sin demora a la persona adecuada.

questions.question: A customer asks whether a form is mandatory. Which reply is clear and appropriately neutral?
options: The form is obligatory for every request except urgencies that are treated by separate.
The form is required in standard petitions, but urgency cases can manage in another way.
The form is required for standard requests, but urgent cases can be handled separately.
You must always fill the form, unless we decide an urgent case does not need it at all.
questions.explanation: «Is required for» expresa un requisito con tono neutral. «Can be handled separately» usa una pasiva natural para describir la excepción.
questions.translation: El formulario es obligatorio para las solicitudes estándar, pero los casos urgentes pueden tramitarse por separado.

questions.question: Which sentence explains a technical dependency in plain English?
options: The check relies in having available the audit registers along the period reviewed.
The check relies on audit logs being available for the period under review.
The checking has dependency of audit logs availability for the reviewed period.
The check depends that audit logs are available during the period in revision.
questions.explanation: «Rely on + sustantivo/gerundio» es la estructura correcta. «The period under review» es una fórmula compacta y profesional.
questions.translation: La comprobación depende de que estén disponibles los registros de auditoría del periodo examinado.

questions.question: You want to confirm that all prerequisites are in place. Which question is most natural?
options: Do we have everything we need to move forward?
Are all the needed prerequisites already disposed for continuing?
Do we have all what we need for moving forward with the process?
Have we everything necessary to advance forward?
questions.explanation: «Everything we need to move forward» es una pregunta breve y natural. «All what» y «advance forward» no son idiomáticos.
questions.translation: ¿Tenemos todo lo necesario para seguir adelante?

questions.question: An approval is still missing. Choose the best status sentence.
options: We have readiness to continue once the pending approbation would be received.
We are prepared to proceed immediately when the rest approval arrives to us.
We are ready for proceeding as soon as we will receive the approval that remains.
We are ready to proceed as soon as we receive the remaining approval.
questions.explanation: Después de «as soon as» se usa presente simple. «Remaining approval» identifica el elemento pendiente de forma natural.
questions.translation: Estamos listos para continuar en cuanto recibamos la aprobación pendiente.

questions.question: You need to state that a step is recommended but not compulsory. Which sentence is best?
options: A brief check of backup should be done, although nobody is forced for doing it.
It is recommended to make a backup check, but this step is not of obligation.
A brief backup check is recommendable, despite it is not an obligated step.
A brief backup check is recommended, although it is not a mandatory step.
questions.explanation: «Is recommended» y «is not mandatory» distinguen claramente recomendación y obligación. «Despite» no introduce directamente una oración con verbo.
questions.translation: Se recomienda una breve comprobación de la copia de seguridad, aunque no es un paso obligatorio.

questions.topic: Explaining processes · Progress and current status
questions.question: A customer asks where the case stands. Which update sounds most natural?
options: The case is being revised actually, and no blockage has been found for the time being yet.
The case is currently under review, and we have not identified any blockers so far.
The case is actually in revision, and we did not identify blockers until the moment.
Currently the case finds itself under reviewing, without blockers identified up to now.
questions.explanation: «Currently under review» y «so far» son expresiones naturales para el estado actual. «Actually» significa «en realidad», no «actualmente».
questions.translation: El caso está actualmente en revisión y, hasta ahora, no hemos identificado ningún bloqueo.

questions.topic: Explaining processes · Progress and current status
questions.question: Complete the update: 'We have completed the initial checks and are now ___ the results.'
options: reviewed
reviewing
review
to reviewing
questions.explanation: Después de «are now» se usa el participio presente para una acción en curso: «are now reviewing».
questions.translation: Hemos completado las comprobaciones iniciales y ahora estamos revisando los resultados.

questions.topic: Explaining processes · Progress and current status
questions.question: Which sentence clearly distinguishes completed work from ongoing work?
options: Collection of data is completed, while analysis keeps being presently on course.
The data was collected already, but the analysis is yet progressing actually.
The data collection is complete, while the analysis is still in progress.
The data collection has finished, meanwhile the analysis still continues in progress.
questions.explanation: «Is complete» contrasta de forma limpia con «is still in progress». «While» une dos oraciones; «meanwhile» requeriría otra puntuación.
questions.translation: La recopilación de datos ha finalizado, mientras que el análisis sigue en curso.

questions.topic: Explaining processes · Progress and current status
questions.question: You need to report progress without suggesting that the work is nearly finished. Which sentence is best?
options: We are almost finished, although there are various items to review yet.
We have advanced a lot, but several points remain for being revised.
The process has progressed and soon all remaining items will definitely be completed.
We have made progress, but several items still need to be reviewed.
questions.explanation: «Have made progress» informa de avance sin cuantificarlo. «Still need to be reviewed» describe trabajo pendiente sin prometer una finalización próxima.
questions.translation: Hemos avanzado, pero todavía hay que revisar varios elementos.

questions.topic: Explaining processes · Progress and current status
questions.question: A task was delayed earlier but is moving again. Choose the most natural update.
options: The issue resolved; work is back in track.
The issue has been resolved, and the work is now back on track.
The incidence is solved, and now the works are back in the correct way.
The issue has resolved, and the work has returned again to its normal track.
questions.explanation: La pasiva «has been resolved» indica un resultado reciente. «Back on track» es la expresión idiomática para decir que el trabajo vuelve a avanzar según lo previsto.
questions.translation: El problema se ha resuelto y el trabajo vuelve a avanzar según lo previsto.

questions.topic: Explaining processes · Progress and current status
questions.question: Which sentence is appropriate when there has been no material change since the last update?
options: There has been no significant change since our last update.
No relevant change happened since the previous information we made to you.
There was not any significative change from our last actualization.
There has not been changes of significance since we updated you the last time.
questions.explanation: El present perfect con «since» conecta el último informe con el presente. «Significant» es el adjetivo correcto; «significative» no es habitual.
questions.translation: No ha habido ningún cambio significativo desde nuestra última actualización.

questions.topic: Explaining processes · Progress and current status
questions.question: You want to mention a small delay without sounding defensive. Which wording is best?
options: We are delayed due to we need validating one additional group of datas.
The review is taking slightly longer than expected because we are validating an additional data set.
The review has a little retard because of an additional dataset that we must validate it.
The review takes more time than expected because an extra data is being validated.
questions.explanation: «Is taking slightly longer than expected» comunica el retraso con neutralidad. «Because» introduce una oración y «data set» evita tratar «data» como «an extra data».
questions.translation: La revisión está tardando un poco más de lo previsto porque estamos validando un conjunto de datos adicional.

questions.topic: Explaining processes · Progress and current status
questions.question: Which question checks progress in a polite, non-pressuring way?
options: Could you let us know how the internal review is progressing?
Can you tell us why the internal review is not finished still?
Could you inform us how is progressing the internal revision?
We would like knowing in which point does the internal review find itself.
questions.explanation: En una pregunta indirecta se mantiene el orden afirmativo: «how the review is progressing». «Could you let us know» suaviza la petición.
questions.translation: ¿Podrían indicarnos cómo avanza la revisión interna?

questions.topic: Explaining processes · Progress and current status
questions.question: A colleague says, 'We finished most of it.' Which customer-facing version is more precise?
options: We finished almost checks, and two are remaining to make.
Most planned checkings are already finalized except two that stay open yet.
Most of the planned checks have been completed, and two remain outstanding.
The majority of checks have completed, with two still being pendent.
questions.explanation: «Have been completed» usa la pasiva correcta y «remain outstanding» identifica tareas pendientes. «Pendent» es un falso amigo.
questions.translation: Se han completado la mayoría de las comprobaciones previstas y quedan dos pendientes.

questions.topic: Explaining processes · Progress and current status
questions.question: You need to explain that you are waiting but still doing useful work. Which sentence is clearest?
options: While we wait for approval, we are preparing the implementation checklist.
During we wait for approval, we prepare the checklist of implementation.
While waiting the approval, we are making ready the list for implementing.
Meanwhile of the approval, the implementation checklist is in preparation by us.
questions.explanation: «While we wait» introduce una acción simultánea. La colocación es «wait for approval» y «prepare a checklist».
questions.translation: Mientras esperamos la aprobación, estamos preparando la lista de comprobación para la implantación.

questions.question: You are explaining when a case is passed to another team. Which sentence is most natural?
options: If specialist input is needed, we hand the case over to the engineering team.
If a specialist input is needed, we hand over the case toward engineering team.
If specialist support will be necessary, we pass the case for the engineers team.
In case of needing specialist inputs, the case is derived to the team of engineering.
questions.explanation: «Hand something over to someone» describe un traspaso de forma natural. «Input» es incontable y en una condición no se usa «will» de este modo.
questions.translation: Si se necesita la aportación de un especialista, transferimos el caso al equipo de ingeniería.

questions.question: Complete the sentence: 'The case is escalated ___ the on-call manager when the agreed criteria are met.'
options: The case is escalated for the on-call manager when the criteria are met.
The case is escalated towards of the on-call manager when the criteria are met.
The case is escalated to the on-call manager when the criteria are met.
The case is escalated at the on-call manager when the criteria are met.
questions.explanation: La preposición habitual es «escalate something to someone»: «the case is escalated to the manager».
questions.translation: El caso se escala al responsable de guardia cuando se cumplen los criterios acordados.

questions.question: Which sentence explains escalation without making it sound like a failure?
options: Escalating is only for putting more expert knowledge when the next stage will need it.
Escalation simply brings in the additional expertise needed for the next stage.
Escalation means the first team failed and another expert must repair the process.
The escalation supposes to incorporate experts because the process went wrongly.
questions.explanation: «Brings in additional expertise» presenta el escalado como incorporación de apoyo. «Needed for the next stage» explica la finalidad sin culpar al primer equipo.
questions.translation: El escalado simplemente incorpora los conocimientos adicionales necesarios para la siguiente fase.

questions.question: You need to describe a smooth transfer of information. Choose the best sentence.
options: The case annotations are shared for giving full context to the team who receives it.
We share to the receiver team the case notes for that they have all the context.
We send the notes with the team that receives, so they can know the context completely.
We share the case notes with the receiving team so that they have the full context.
questions.explanation: «Share something with someone» es la estructura correcta. «So that» introduce la finalidad y «receiving team» es una expresión compacta.
questions.translation: Compartimos las notas del caso con el equipo receptor para que disponga de todo el contexto.

questions.question: A customer asks whether they must repeat all the details after a handoff. Which reply sounds most reassuring?
options: It should not be necessary that you repeat us the context, as we will include it on handover.
You will not have to repeat nothing because we put every background in the transfer notes.
You should not need to repeat the background, as we will include it in the handover notes.
You do not need repeating all details since the notes of handoff will contain them already.
questions.explanation: «Should not need to» tranquiliza sin prometer de forma absoluta. No se usa doble negación, y «include it in the notes» lleva «in».
questions.translation: En principio no tendrán que repetir los antecedentes, ya que los incluiremos en las notas de traspaso.

questions.question: Which sentence clearly states who remains the customer's contact after an internal escalation?
options: Although internally escalated, your main contact will keep being ourselves.
Despite the case has escalated internally, we continue being your principal contact point.
Although the case has been escalated internally, we will remain your main point of contact.
Even the case is in escalation, we remain as the contact point more important for you.
questions.explanation: «Although + oración» introduce el contraste correctamente. «Remain your main point of contact» no necesita «as» y suena profesional.
questions.translation: Aunque el caso se ha escalado internamente, seguiremos siendo su principal punto de contacto.

questions.question: You want to introduce the next speaker after explaining your team's part. What should you say?
options: I now hand to Priya to explain implementation.
Now I pass with Priya, who is going to explain about the implementation phase.
I will hand the meeting to Priya so she explains us the implementing stage.
I will now hand over to Priya, who will explain the implementation stage.
questions.explanation: «Hand over to [persona]» es una fórmula habitual para ceder la palabra. «Explain» no lleva «about» cuando tiene un objeto directo.
questions.translation: Ahora cedo la palabra a Priya, que explicará la fase de implantación.

questions.question: A handoff is delayed because the receiving team needs more context. Which update is best?
options: Handover is in pending because the team that receives needs that we give more explanations.
The transfer waits until we are giving to the receiving team more context.
The handoff is pendent while we provide additional context to the team receiver.
The handoff is pending while we provide the receiving team with additional context.
questions.explanation: «Is pending while...» describe el estado y la acción en curso. La estructura correcta es «provide someone with something».
questions.translation: El traspaso está pendiente mientras proporcionamos contexto adicional al equipo receptor.

questions.question: Which phrase best introduces an escalation criterion?
options: We escalate the case if it falls outside the team's agreed scope.
We escalate the case in case it will fall out of the scope agreed for the team.
We escalate cases outside from the agreed scope.
The case escalates when it is outside from the team's scope that was accorded.
questions.explanation: «Falls outside the team's agreed scope» es una colocación natural. En la condición se usa presente simple, no «will».
questions.translation: Escalamos el caso si queda fuera del alcance acordado para el equipo.

questions.question: You are closing a handoff call. Which sentence confirms continuity most clearly?
options: The new team received case detail and is going to pick the investigation where we let it.
The new team has the details and retakes from here.
The case details are with the new team, which will continue on the investigation since here.
The new team has the case details and will pick up the investigation from here.
questions.explanation: «Pick up the investigation from here» indica continuidad de forma idiomática. Evita las traducciones literales «retake» y «since here».
questions.translation: El nuevo equipo dispone de los detalles del caso y continuará la investigación a partir de este punto.

questions.question: You need to give an estimate rather than a promise. Which sentence is best?
options: We expect the review to take approximately two business days.
We expect the review to last two labor days.
We promise the review will be finished exactly within two working days.
We expect that the review takes around two labor days approximately.
questions.explanation: «Expect something to take...» expresa una estimación. «Approximately» y «business days» son naturales; la frase evita convertir la estimación en promesa.
questions.translation: Prevemos que la revisión tarde aproximadamente dos días laborables.

questions.question: Complete the update: 'We aim to send you the draft ___ Friday.'
options: We aim to send you the draft until Friday.
We aim to send you the draft by Friday.
We aim to send you the draft in Friday.
We aim to send you the draft at Friday.
questions.explanation: «By Friday» significa «a más tardar el viernes». «Until Friday» describe continuidad hasta ese día, no una fecha límite de entrega.
questions.translation: Nuestro objetivo es enviarles el borrador a más tardar el viernes.

questions.question: Which sentence sets a realistic expectation about timing?
options: Timing can suffer changes if it would be necessary to validate additionally.
The timeline may change if additional validation is required.
The planning may modify itself in case more validation will be required.
The timeline changes if validation would be needed.
questions.explanation: «May change if...» expresa una posibilidad real. En la cláusula con «if» se usa presente simple: «if ... is required».
questions.translation: El calendario puede cambiar si se requiere una validación adicional.

questions.question: A customer asks for an exact completion time, but you do not have one. Which reply is most professional?
options: I do not have an exact timing for now; nevertheless, this afternoon I will inform you with more details.
I cannot say the exact hour, but surely it will be completed this afternoon.
Still I cannot confirm you when exactly, but I can actualize you later today.
I cannot confirm an exact time yet, but I can give you a further update this afternoon.
questions.explanation: «Cannot confirm ... yet» explica la limitación y «give you a further update» ofrece un siguiente paso concreto. No promete la finalización.
questions.translation: Todavía no puedo confirmar una hora exacta, pero esta tarde podré darles otra actualización.

questions.question: Which sentence explains a service target in plain language?
options: Our target is to acknowledge urgent requests within 30 minutes.
Our target is acknowledging urgencies inside 30 minutes.
Our target consists in acknowledging the urgent petitions inside of 30 minutes.
We have as target to give acknowledgement of urgencies in a lapse of 30 minutes.
questions.explanation: «Our target is to...» y «within 30 minutes» expresan el objetivo con claridad. «Within» significa que la acción se realizará antes de que termine ese plazo.
questions.translation: Nuestro objetivo es acusar recibo de las solicitudes urgentes en un plazo de 30 minutos.

questions.question: You need to distinguish response time from resolution time. Choose the clearest wording.
options: The target of two hours applies for responding initially, but not for resolving finally.
The two-hour compromise concerns initial answering instead of definitive solution time.
The two-hour target applies to our initial response, not to the final resolution.
Two hours is the objective for first response and does not mean the case resolves then.
questions.explanation: «Applies to» es la preposición correcta. El contraste «initial response, not ... final resolution» evita ambigüedad; «compromise» es un falso amigo.
questions.translation: El objetivo de dos horas se aplica a nuestra respuesta inicial, no a la resolución final.

questions.question: A delivery depends on receiving feedback today. Which sentence is appropriately conditional?
options: If we will receive your feedback today, we can finalize the document tomorrow for sure.
Receiving today your feedback, we would definitely finish the document by tomorrow.
If we receive your feedback today, we should be able to finalize the document tomorrow.
If we received your feedback today, tomorrow the document should can be finalized.
questions.explanation: En una condición real se usa presente simple tras «if». «Should be able to» comunica una previsión razonable sin garantía absoluta.
questions.translation: Si recibimos hoy sus comentarios, en principio podremos finalizar el documento mañana.

questions.question: Which phrase is most natural when a date is provisional?
options: We have pencilled in the change for 18 November, subject to approval.
The provisional change date stays in 18 November, subordinated at receiving approval.
We have written the change in pencil for 18 November, depending of the approbation.
We scheduled definitively the change on 18 November unless approval could be missing.
questions.explanation: «Pencil something in» significa programarlo de manera provisional. «Subject to approval» deja clara la condición pendiente.
questions.translation: Hemos previsto provisionalmente el cambio para el 18 de noviembre, sujeto a aprobación.

questions.question: You want to explain that a date is unchanged. Which update is best?
options: We are yet according to schedule to finish all work before the week will end.
The planning maintains for finishing the works at the week's ending.
We are still on schedule to complete the work by the end of the week.
We continue in schedule for completing the work until the end of the week.
questions.explanation: «On schedule» indica que se mantiene el calendario. «By the end of the week» señala la fecha límite; «until» no expresa lo mismo.
questions.translation: Seguimos dentro del calendario previsto para completar el trabajo antes de que termine la semana.

questions.question: A timeline has slipped. Which sentence communicates the change and the next update clearly?
options: The completion date has displaced until Monday, and tomorrow we confirm the new planning.
The finishing date moved on Monday, while the revised plan will be confirmed in tomorrow.
The completion date has moved to Monday, and we will confirm the revised plan tomorrow.
There is a delay to Monday; tomorrow we will assure you the planning that was revised.
questions.explanation: «Has moved to Monday» comunica el cambio con neutralidad. «Confirm the revised plan tomorrow» usa las preposiciones y el orden natural.
questions.translation: La fecha de finalización se ha trasladado al lunes y mañana confirmaremos el plan revisado.

questions.topic: Next steps · Actions, owners and deadlines
questions.question: You are summarizing the first action after a meeting. Which sentence is clearest?
options: As first following step, we will make the verification of the affected device list.
The first step is verifying the affected devices listing.
The first thing next is verifying which devices are affected in the listing.
The first step is to verify the list of affected devices.
questions.explanation: «The first step is to + infinitive» es una estructura clara y evita la redundancia de «first next step». «Affected devices» coloca el adjetivo antes del sustantivo.
questions.translation: El primer paso es verificar la lista de dispositivos afectados.

questions.topic: Next steps · Actions, owners and deadlines
questions.question: Complete the action summary: 'Marta will update the runbook ___ 13 November.'
options: Marta will update the runbook on maximum 13 November.
Marta will update the runbook inside 13 November.
Marta will update the runbook until 13 November.
Marta will update the runbook by 13 November.
questions.explanation: «By 13 November» marca una fecha límite. «Until» indicaría que la acción continúa hasta ese día.
questions.translation: Marta actualizará el runbook a más tardar el 13 de noviembre.

questions.topic: Next steps · Actions, owners and deadlines
questions.question: Which sentence records an owner and an action in the most concise way?
options: Daniel takes as action to confirm about the maintenance window to infrastructure team.
The confirmation of maintenance window has Daniel as its action owner for the team.
Daniel will confirm the maintenance window with the infrastructure team.
Daniel confirms about the maintenance window.
questions.explanation: Una cláusula activa con nombre + «will» + verbo registra responsable y acción sin rodeos. «Confirm» no necesita «about».
questions.translation: Daniel confirmará la ventana de mantenimiento con el equipo de infraestructura.

questions.topic: Next steps · Actions, owners and deadlines
questions.question: You need to propose, not impose, the next action. Which wording is best?
options: My suggestion is that tomorrow we are obliged to make a joint revision.
I suggest that we review the open items together tomorrow.
I suggest us to review open items tomorrow.
I propose that you must review all open points with us tomorrow.
questions.explanation: Después de «suggest that», se usa la forma base: «we review». La propuesta colaborativa evita «must» y «obliged».
questions.translation: Sugiero que mañana revisemos juntos los elementos pendientes.

questions.topic: Next steps · Actions, owners and deadlines
questions.question: A customer action is optional. Which sentence communicates that clearly?
options: If useful, your team can comment in the document.
In case of utility, comments may be put by your team inside the sharing document.
If useful, your team can add comments directly to the shared document.
Your team can add comments directly on the document if you will find it useful.
questions.explanation: «If useful» y «can» presentan la acción como opcional. «Shared document» es el adjetivo correcto, no «sharing document».
questions.translation: Si les resulta útil, su equipo puede añadir comentarios directamente en el documento compartido.

questions.topic: Next steps · Actions, owners and deadlines
questions.question: Which question confirms ownership without sounding confrontational?
options: Do you accept to lead this action that nobody else is owning?
Are you comfortable taking the lead on this action?
Will you take this action because it belongs to your side?
Are you disposed to lead this action?
questions.explanation: «Are you comfortable + gerundio?» comprueba disponibilidad con tacto. «Take the lead on» es una colocación profesional.
questions.translation: ¿Les parece bien liderar esta acción?

questions.topic: Next steps · Actions, owners and deadlines
questions.question: You want to leave a deadline open for agreement. Which sentence is best?
options: We can accord a deadline after estimating effort.
We will define a final date when the estimation of efforts would be already done.
We can accord a convenient due date once the effort will be estimated.
We can agree a suitable deadline once the effort has been estimated.
questions.explanation: «Agree a suitable deadline» y «once ... has been estimated» son naturales. En la subordinada temporal no se usa «will».
questions.translation: Podemos acordar un plazo adecuado una vez que se haya estimado el esfuerzo.

questions.topic: Next steps · Actions, owners and deadlines
questions.question: Which sentence makes the dependency between two next steps explicit?
options: When the scope would be approved from you, the final plan can get prepared by us.
Once you will approve, we prepare the final plan.
Once you will approve the scope, we can prepare the definitive plan of implementation.
Once you approve the scope, we can prepare the final implementation plan.
questions.explanation: Tras «once» se usa presente simple. La estructura muestra con claridad que la preparación depende de la aprobación.
questions.translation: Una vez que aprueben el alcance, podremos preparar el plan de implantación definitivo.

questions.topic: Next steps · Actions, owners and deadlines
questions.question: A meeting produced several actions. How should you introduce them in writing?
options: In the following you can find summarized the actions with who owns and when due.
Below is a resume of actions, owners and dates.
Below is a summary of the agreed actions, owners and due dates.
Down below are the agreements of action, their proprietary people and deadline dates.
questions.explanation: «Below is a summary of...» es una apertura estándar. «Agreed actions, owners and due dates» usa términos profesionales concisos; «resume» y «responsibles» son falsos amigos.
questions.translation: A continuación figura un resumen de las acciones acordadas, sus responsables y las fechas límite.

questions.topic: Next steps · Actions, owners and deadlines
questions.question: You need to confirm that no action is required from the customer yet. Which sentence is clearest?
options: Your team has not an action in this moment; we contact you if an input will be needed.
There is no action for your team at this stage; we will contact you when input is needed.
No action is required from your side for now, until we will ask something from you.
At this stage you do not need doing anything; we advise when your collaboration becomes necessary.
questions.explanation: «There is no action for your team at this stage» es claro y neutral. Tras «when» con sentido futuro se usa presente simple.
questions.translation: En esta fase su equipo no tiene que realizar ninguna acción; nos pondremos en contacto cuando necesitemos su aportación.

questions.question: You need to identify a blocker without assigning blame. Which sentence is best?
options: The next step is blocked because your team did not give us the access we asked for.
There is a blockage since we continue without receiving access from your side.
The next step is currently blocked because the required access has not yet been granted.
The process cannot advance due to the access is still not granted by the responsible people.
questions.explanation: La pasiva «has not yet been granted» centra el mensaje en el requisito pendiente, no en culpar a una persona. «Because» introduce correctamente la oración.
questions.translation: El siguiente paso está actualmente bloqueado porque todavía no se ha concedido el acceso necesario.

questions.question: Complete the contingency statement: 'If the primary contact is unavailable, we will reach out ___ the backup contact.'
options: We will reach out with the backup contact.
We will reach out at the backup contact.
We will reach out to the backup contact.
We will reach out towards the backup contact.
questions.explanation: La expresión correcta es «reach out to someone», que significa ponerse en contacto con alguien.
questions.translation: Si el contacto principal no está disponible, nos pondremos en contacto con la persona de respaldo.

questions.question: Which sentence proposes a workaround clearly and cautiously?
options: Like workaround in the meantime, we can use the logs while access is recuperated again.
As a temporary workaround, we can use the exported logs until direct access is restored.
For a provisional solution, exported registers can substitute perfectly the direct access.
As temporal workaround, we will use exported logs until direct access will restore.
questions.explanation: «As a temporary workaround» introduce una solución provisional. Tras «until» se usa presente simple y «restored» es el verbo natural para el acceso.
questions.translation: Como solución temporal, podemos utilizar los registros exportados hasta que se restablezca el acceso directo.

questions.question: A risk may affect the timeline, but it has not caused a delay yet. Choose the best update.
options: This may affect the timeline, although it has not caused any delay so far.
This is delaying the timeline, although until now no delay has happened.
The timeline will probably be delayed by this risk, even no delay exists currently.
This could affect to the planning, despite it did not cause a delay yet.
questions.explanation: «May affect» describe un riesgo, no un hecho. «Although» introduce una oración y «so far» combina bien con present perfect.
questions.translation: Esto puede afectar al calendario, aunque hasta ahora no ha causado ningún retraso.

questions.question: You need to ask for help removing a blocker. Which request sounds most collaborative?
options: Could your team help us confirm the correct access group?
Could your team help confirming the correct group?
Can your team solve the blocker by telling us which access group is correct?
We need that your team helps us to confirm which is the group of correct access.
questions.explanation: «Could your team help us + verbo?» es una petición colaborativa. En la pregunta indirecta se usa «the correct access group», sin inversión.
questions.translation: ¿Podría su equipo ayudarnos a confirmar cuál es el grupo de acceso correcto?

questions.question: Which sentence explains what will happen if a dependency is not met?
options: If approval will not be received until noon, we move the change at the following window available.
If approval is not received by noon, we will move the change to the next available window.
Without approval by noon, the change would pass to the next window that will be available.
If we do not receive the approbation at noon, we delay the change for next possible maintenance.
questions.explanation: En el primer condicional se usa presente simple tras «if» y «will» en la consecuencia. «Move ... to the next available window» es natural y preciso.
questions.translation: Si no se recibe la aprobación antes del mediodía, trasladaremos el cambio a la siguiente ventana disponible.

questions.question: A blocker has been removed. Which update is most natural?
options: Access is granted, so we can retake validation.
They granted the access, therefore we can retake again the validation from now.
The access has been given now, so we can restart again with validation works.
Access has now been granted, so we can resume the validation work.
questions.explanation: «Has now been granted» destaca el cambio reciente. «Resume the work» ya implica continuar y no necesita «again».
questions.translation: Ya se ha concedido el acceso, por lo que podemos reanudar el trabajo de validación.

questions.question: You want to distinguish a blocker from a minor issue. Which sentence is clearest?
options: We should track this issue, although it is not blocking us for continuing forward.
This issue needs to be tracked, but it does not prevent us from continuing.
This incidence needs following, but it does not avoid us to continue.
This issue has to be controlled, but it does not impede that we continue with the process.
questions.explanation: La estructura es «prevent someone from + gerundio». «Needs to be tracked» comunica seguimiento sin presentar el problema como bloqueo.
questions.translation: Hay que hacer seguimiento de este problema, pero no nos impide continuar.

questions.question: A fallback plan exists. Which sentence introduces it most professionally?
options: If the preferred option would not be available, our plan B consists in using the manual process.
If the preferred option is not available, our fallback is to use the manual process.
If there is no availability of the option preferred, the alternative is make a manual processing.
In case the favourite option fails, we fall back with doing the process manually.
questions.explanation: «If ... is not available» usa una condición real, y «our fallback is to...» presenta la alternativa con claridad. «Consist» llevaría «in».
questions.translation: Si la opción preferida no está disponible, nuestra alternativa es utilizar el proceso manual.

questions.question: You need to say that no contingency action is required now. Choose the best wording.
options: We are monitoring the situation, but there is no need to activate the contingency plan at this point.
The situation is controlled, so the contingency plan will never need to be activated.
We are making monitoring of the situation, although there is no necessity for activating the contingency plan in this moment.
We are making monitoring, although there is no necessity to activate contingency in this point.
questions.explanation: «There is no need to + infinitive» es la estructura natural. «At this point» limita la afirmación al momento actual sin descartar cambios futuros.
questions.translation: Estamos supervisando la situación, pero en este momento no es necesario activar el plan de contingencia.

questions.question: You are ending a process explanation. Which sentence provides the clearest recap?
options: For recapitulating, we will validate all data, investigate the findings and then share to you our recommendations.
For recapitulating, we validate the data, investigate findings and will share recommendations.
To recap, we will validate the data, investigate the findings and share our recommendations.
To resume, there will be validation, investigation and a sharing of our recommendations.
questions.explanation: «To recap» introduce un resumen de forma natural. Los tres verbos en futuro mantienen el paralelismo: «will validate, investigate and share».
questions.translation: En resumen, validaremos los datos, investigaremos los hallazgos y compartiremos nuestras recomendaciones.

questions.question: Complete the closing question: 'Does that give you a clear picture ___ what happens next?'
options: Does that give you a clear picture for what happens next?
Does that give you a clear picture on what happens next?
Does that give you a clear picture about of what happens next?
Does that give you a clear picture of what happens next?
questions.explanation: La colocación es «a clear picture of something». No se combina «about» con «of».
questions.translation: ¿Les da esto una idea clara de lo que ocurre a continuación?

questions.question: Which sentence invites questions about the workflow in a natural way?
options: Before moving to the following point, do you have any doubt about some part of this process to clarify?
Before moving forward, do you have any doubt about some part of the process?
Prior to continue, is there a process part that you want I clarify?
Before we move on, is there any part of the process you would like me to clarify?
questions.explanation: «Would like me to clarify» usa la estructura «would like + persona + to + verbo». En inglés profesional suele decirse «questions», no «doubts», para invitar consultas.
questions.translation: Antes de continuar, ¿hay alguna parte del proceso que quieran que aclare?

questions.question: You want to check agreement on the next steps. Which question is most professional?
options: Are everybody in alignment on the actions and their proprietary persons agreed now?
Are we all aligned on the actions and owners we have just discussed?
Do all of us agree ourselves with actions and who must make each one?
Are we all aligned about the actions and responsibles that we just accorded?
questions.explanation: «Be aligned on» es una colocación profesional y «actions and owners» resume qué y quién. «We have just discussed» evita repetir «agreed» en la misma frase.
questions.translation: ¿Estamos todos de acuerdo con las acciones y los responsables que acabamos de tratar?

questions.question: A customer asks for a written record of the next steps. Which reply is best?
options: Of course. I will send you a writing summary when the call will finish.
Yes, I send a written resume posterior to the call.
Certainly. After the call ends, a summary in written will be remitted to you.
Of course. I will send a written summary after the call.
questions.explanation: «A written summary» es la expresión natural. Tras «after» con referencia futura se usa presente simple: «after the call» o «after the call ends».
questions.translation: Por supuesto. Enviaré un resumen por escrito después de la llamada.

questions.question: Which closing sentence combines the immediate next step with a future update?
options: We start today the validation and will update you once results will be available initially.
We are going to initiate validation today, then inform you when the initial result would be ready.
Validation will be started today, and when available the first results we actualize you.
We will start the validation today and update you once the initial results are available.
questions.explanation: La frase mantiene dos acciones paralelas con «will». Tras «once» se usa presente simple: «once ... are available».
questions.translation: Empezaremos hoy la validación y les informaremos cuando estén disponibles los resultados iniciales.

questions.question: You need to mention an unresolved point in the recap. Which sentence is clearest?
options: Only remains open the final date, which will be confirmed posterior to meeting for approval.
The only open point is the final date, which we will confirm after the approval meeting.
The final date is the only point pendent and we will confirm it after approval will meet.
The unique open point is the definitive date, that we confirm after the approbation meeting.
questions.explanation: «The only open point is...» destaca el asunto pendiente. La oración de relativo con «which» y «after the meeting» suena natural.
questions.translation: El único punto pendiente es la fecha definitiva, que confirmaremos después de la reunión de aprobación.

questions.question: Which sentence closes the meeting without implying that every detail is final?
options: With this all planning is covered, although details can refine while work will progress.
That closes the definitive plan, and details will be changed if problems appear.
That covers the current plan; we can refine the details as the work progresses.
This is all about the plan for now; later we make more precise its details during advancement.
questions.explanation: «The current plan» limita el alcance y «as the work progresses» permite ajustes. «Refine the details» es una colocación natural.
questions.translation: Eso cubre el plan actual; podemos precisar los detalles a medida que avance el trabajo.

questions.question: You want to confirm the date of the next checkpoint. What is the most natural question?
options: Do we put the next control meeting in Tuesday by the morning?
Shall we program the check-in in Tuesday?
Are we scheduling next checkpoint at Tuesday in the morning time?
Shall we schedule the next check-in for Tuesday morning?
questions.explanation: «Shall we...?» propone una acción conjunta. Para días se usa «on», pero con «Tuesday morning» tras «for» no hace falta artículo.
questions.translation: ¿Programamos la próxima reunión de seguimiento para el martes por la mañana?

questions.question: A customer confirms the plan. Which final response sounds warm and professional?
options: Excellent, thank you. We continue as we spoke and will keep you information.
Great, thank you. We will proceed as agreed and keep you informed.
Perfect, thanks. We proceed like accorded and maintain you informed.
Very good. We will advance according the agreement and keep informing to you.
questions.explanation: «Proceed as agreed» y «keep you informed» son fórmulas profesionales naturales. «According» necesitaría «to» y «inform» no lleva «to» ante la persona.
questions.translation: Perfecto, gracias. Procederemos según lo acordado y les mantendremos informados.
